by: session, Adrian 16 Oct 2026: 'put each common mistake at the end of its clip as a Watch out step' — here rejecting x = -1 is the method, so it stays in place as a plain reason

beats.say: Solve log base three of X minus eight equals two minus log base three of X.
The plan: get one log on each side, then compare what is inside.

do.text: Aim: one log each side, then compare

asks: Why one log on each side?

beats.say: Move minus log base three of X to the left. It becomes plus log base three of X.
Add Power joins the two logs: log of X times the bracket X minus eight.
asks: What is the Add Power law?

beats.say: Write two as log base three of nine. Three squared is nine.
One log each side: drop the logs. X times the bracket equals nine, so X squared minus eight X minus nine equals zero.
asks: Why can I drop the logs?

beats.say: Factorise. X minus nine, times X plus one, equals zero.
So X equals nine or X equals minus one.
Check every root in the logs. X equals minus one gives log of minus nine, so reject it.
The answer is X equals nine.
